transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-27 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Jordan Alvarez, Priya Singh (Redwood); Liam O'Neill, Sara Gomez, Derek Wu, Anita Rao (BeaconMart)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through the containment and then hand off the trigger analysis, um, i'm maya, i'm your AE, and jordan from engineering will take the deep dive 
[00:30] Liam O'Neill: cool, thanks maya, appreciate it, we had a bad spike last month that bubbled up into customer complaints so want to make sure we close the loop
[01:05] Priya Singh: quick agenda — incident summary, current containment, root-cause hypotheses, remediation proposals, handoff actions — and time for security questions
[01:40] Sara Gomez: for context, we observed repeated p99 token latency spikes around 2026-12-18 02:14 UTC, about 12 minutes of elevated latencies, some 5xxs at the storefront — we throttled traffic to dedicated pool which helped but still worried about recurrence
[02:10] Jordan Alvarez: right, from our side we ingested the traces you shared, thanks, and ran a sampling pass — i have three initial vectors: small KV-cache eviction storms, oversized continuous batching interaction, and a model variant fallback that retried too aggressively
[02:50] Derek Wu: can you explain the KV thing — we use prefix caching heavily — is that the K-V cash you mean?
[03:05] Jordan Alvarez: yeah sorry, i said K-V cash — so the prefix cache (kv) experienced eviction cascades when several large requests coincided with a cache compaction job — we saw transient cache miss storms which forced longer decode paths
[03:40] Anita Rao: and that lines up with the timeline of our compaction cron?
[03:55] Sara Gomez: yes, compaction runs at 02:10 UTC normally, we had an overlap with a marketing batch at 02:08, so maybe coincidental
[04:20] Maya Chen: important to note, Redwood Dedicated had the fallback policy configured on that pool — on overflow we fall back to a cheaper model variant and then to region fallback if needed — that fallback's retry window may have compounded latency in some cases
[04:50] Liam O'Neill: so two things — cache eviction plus fallback retries, seems plausible. can you quantify how much the retry added?
[05:20] Jordan Alvarez: rough numbers from traces: about 30% of elevated requests issued a fallback retry; of those, median added ~120ms or more depending on model size, p99s added multiple seconds. when you multiply by the batching window it bumps the headroom down
[05:55] Sara Gomez: there's also some network jitter between our VPC and the Redwood region — not huge but adds variance, could push borderline calls over the threshold
[06:25] Derek Wu: security question — during elevated latencies were logs or payloads retained longer? we need to prove no PII persisted beyond our retention 
[06:45] Priya Singh: we reviewed retention policy — Redwood Console shows request-level audit logs, and the Dedicated pool was configured with short retention; we'll include proof artifacts. derek, we'll send the redacted traces 
[07:20] Jordan Alvarez: i want to walk through the sequence we reconstructed — starting at compaction job -> cache misses -> bigger batches forming -> fallback retries -> burst on dedicated pool -> throttle leading to 5xxs. i can share a sequence diagram after this
[08:05] Liam O'Neill: ok, what immediate mitigations can we do to avoid recurrence? we need actions that don't require major infra work
[08:30] Jordan Alvarez: short term: 1) disable compaction during heavy traffic windows or shift cron, 2) tighten fallback retry policy (reduce retries and add jitter), 3) temporarily increase dedicated pool headroom or enable burst capacity, 4) reduce batch window from 50ms to 20ms in the hot path
[09:05] Sara Gomez: we can change cron and reduce batching quickly — changing retries might be trickier because it's global config but doable with canary
[09:30] Maya Chen: we recommend a canary change first on a small dedicated pool with identical workload to validate. we can run a 24h smoke and share metrics. jordan will own the canary plan
[10:00] Jordan Alvarez: yep, i'll draft the canary and baseline metrics: p50/p95/p99, token-per-request cost delta, tail queue length, error rate by route
[10:30] Anita Rao: what about long-term? we want structural fixes not just bandaids
[10:45] Jordan Alvarez: long-term items: introduce soft isolation lanes for critical routes so compaction and batch shaping don't collide; smarter eviction policy (LRU with heartbeat dampening); circuit-breaker that prevents fallback storms by backoff and token-aware throttling; and better observability into KV hit ratios with alerts at 2.5x baseline
[11:30] Liam O'Neill: soft isolation lanes — that sounds like dedicated routing for checkout route?
[11:50] Jordan Alvarez: exactly — route-based isolation where we pin routing for payment/checkout to a small hot pool with stricter batching rules
[12:10] Derek Wu: for compliance, we need the audit log export and SSO details for the time period — SOC 2 evidence, and confirmation that keys used were under our KMS — is Redwood using customer-managed keys for Dedicated?
[12:40] Priya Singh: for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS integration, yes. we'll send a KMS integration guide and the audit export for that window. derek, can you confirm the key policy you require?
[13:05] Derek Wu: need rotation every 90 days, and HSM-backed if possible, with AE logs showing access requests
[13:25] Maya Chen: noted, we'll include HSM notes from our Private docs and the Dedicated configuration options. i'll also include the support ticket history and timeline we kept
[13:50] Jordan Alvarez: i want to call out one oddity — there were a few requests that went through a cross-region fallback then back to primary because of routing flaps; that created duplicate work and extra cost — we should add a de-duplication token on the request id to avoid double-execution in fallback windows
[14:30] Sara Gomez: hmm we can add a client-side idempotency key easily; our SDK already supports that for write paths, but not always for generation calls — we'll audit SDK usage
[15:00] Maya Chen: good place for a note — we'll add an SDK snippet to the follow-up bundle: idempotency-key header guidance
[15:35] Liam O'Neill: can you estimate cost impact of your proposed short-term changes? if we increase pool headroom and reduce batch windows cost might go up
[16:00] Jordan Alvarez: short-term cost delta estimate: enabling 20% burst headroom adds ~12% monthly spend on Dedicated pool for that tenant profile; reducing batch window increases per-token latency cost marginally but decreases p99 failure rate so net customer impact may be positive; we'll include a model spreadsheet with assumptions
[16:40] Anita Rao: customers will push back on cost increases, they want reliability. we need to show clear ROI
[17:00] Maya Chen: agreed — we'll produce a before/after ROI sheet showing reduced customer-facing errors, projected revenue retention, and cost delta. we'll model a 3-month window
[17:30] Sara Gomez: about the canary — what traffic shape should we use? we can re-play production traces to the test tenant
[17:50] Jordan Alvarez: re-play with a 15% sample that preserves burst patterns and compaction overlap. we want to exercise the boundary conditions, not just steady-state
[18:10] Derek Wu: from security standpoint, replay data must be scrubbed — PII removed, tokens redacted
[18:30] Priya Singh: yes we'll provide redaction guidance; maya to attach the redaction checklist
[19:00] Jordan Alvarez: operational checklist for canary: baseline snapshot, burst injection window, KV eviction metric, batch window change, fallback retry change, monitor p99 and error budget, abort thresholds
[19:40] Liam O'Neill: do we have automated rollback if things go sideways in canary?
[19:55] Jordan Alvarez: yes, our rollout supports automatic rollback on configured SLO breach; we'll help configure the thresholds and wire the hooks to your pager system
[20:20] Anita Rao: timeline — when can we start the canary and how long until we see meaningful results?
[20:35] Jordan Alvarez: once we get a test tenant and API key (1-2 business days), canary run for 48 hours gives good signal, but 7 days is ideal for coverage across cron windows
[21:00] Maya Chen: okay timeline: beacon to provision by Feb 1, redwood to run canary Feb 2-4, share results Feb 5, decision Feb 7
[21:25] Sara Gomez: ok that's workable
[21:40] Derek Wu: let's talk SLA and entitlements — if we make these changes will we get a better SLA or at least a runbook insert?
[22:00] Priya Singh: for Dedicated we can add custom runbook pages and augment the SLA with a reliability addendum in the enterprise contract — we'll propose wording in the follow-up
[22:30] Liam O'Neill: competitor angle — BigCloudAI offered us a per-route isolation feature but they couldn't demonstrate their fallback behavior — we want proof this actually mitigates the double-work issue
[22:55] Jordan Alvarez: we'll provide a microbenchmark showing isolation lane preventing compaction-induced misses and a graph of dedupe token efficacy
[23:30] Maya Chen: any other blockers?
[23:40] Anita Rao: procurement asked for cost cap guardrails, so can we set an upper spend cap on burst capacity?
[23:58] Jordan Alvarez: we can set budget alerts and automatic burst disable if spend exceeds threshold — that's part of Redwood Console controls
[24:30] Liam O'Neill: excellent, let's capture questions from security — derek?
[24:40] Derek Wu: need the SOC 2 report location and whether audit logs for that time include requester IPs and KMS access events
[25:05] Priya Singh: we'll attach SOC 2 attestation and provide the audit export CSV; KMS access events will be included where customer-managed keys were used
[25:40] Maya Chen: ok we should close with concrete next steps and owners — priya, can you recap?
[25:55] Priya Singh: recap: mayas will send traces/redaction checklist; jordan will share canary runbook + config; beacon to provision test tenant; derek to confirm KMS policy. follow-up meeting in one week post canary result share
[26:30] Liam O'Neill: sounds good. one last question — what minimal change could we do instantly to stop recurrence if it happens again tonight?
[26:50] Jordan Alvarez: immediate action is to disable compaction schedule and set fallback retries to 0 in the pool for the hot routes — that's a config flip that takes like 15 minutes and is reversible
[27:15] Sara Gomez: do it. i'll coordinate with infra to flip compaction and push a small config change
[27:35] Anita Rao: and notify customers? we prefer a brief note if we do config flips that change behavior
[27:50] Maya Chen: agreed, we can draft a short comms template for you to use
[28:15] Liam O'Neill: thanks all, appreciate the quick action plan — look forward to the canary results
[28:30] Maya Chen: thanks team. end notes: links to artifacts will be in the CRM note and i will upload to the shared drive: Deck: https://redwood.app/s/CRM-43821/canary-plan, Trace bundle: https://redwood.app/s/CRM-43821/traces (redacted), RBAC/KMS guide: https://redwood.app/docs/kms-dedicated
[29:05] (cross talk and wrap up)

Summary (auto):
- Incident probable root cause: cache eviction cascade + aggressive fallback retries compounded by batch windowing and cross-region routing flaps.
- Immediate mitigations: shift compaction cron, temporary reduce fallback retries, enable burst headroom, reduce batch window for hot path.
- Long-term: route-based soft isolation, smarter eviction policy, dedupe token for fallback, improved telemetry and alerts.

Questions noted: SOC 2 export, KMS/HSM confirmation, cost cap guardrails, canary run parameters

References:
- Canary runbook (to be shared)
- Redacted trace bundle (link above)
- Draft ROI spreadsheet (will be attached by maya)

End of transcript.
